description: JVM async/await slice (ISSUE-0099), rebased onto the v1.2 canonical: JVM-only fixtures that run the real DEAL frontend (lexer → parser → module-shape validation → name resolver → type checker) → real JvmBackend codegen → javac → java executing the emitted artifact (the harness fails a fixture whose codegen or JVM execution is bypassed). The slice uses spec-v1.2's permitted JVM blocking-call lowering: an async function compiles to a plain static method returning its declared type; `await E` evaluates the direct call and applies the declared-return-type completion check at the await site (int completions route through checkInt — E8004; number/string/boolean/null completions are proven by the emitted Java types, which §JVM backend contract permits). Async function values reuse the ISSUE-0098 wrapper machinery unchanged — the per-signature wrapper shape class and per-declaration wrapper field cover async markers, and awaited indirect calls dispatch through invoke. Covered forms: async returns, await in value positions (let initializers, return positions, nested call arguments, if conditions), await in discard positions, completion success (value paths, the int safe-range boundary, null completions) and completion failure (an awaited operation completing by raising E8005, propagating through one and two await levels), direct calls with primitive/string/boolean/null signatures, async function values (typed locals, callback parameters, reassigned local bindings), imported async direct calls through the orchestrator multi-module pipeline (the entry module exporting the v1.2 selected-entry non-async main(): null), and three frontend compile-error gates (E3012 await outside async, E3013 await on a sync call, E3014 async call without await) rejected before any backend runs. The JVM guard over reassigned async function-typed locals/parameters descends into awaited calls: an assignment hidden in an awaited call's argument list is a real reassignment, so the adapter over the binding is rejected with E6000 (never a silent snapshot) and the live-read semantics are pinned by one LuaJIT-only reference fixture (the retargeted async adapter computes 11; the async adapter returns the inner operation handle and the completion check stays at the await site). ISSUE-0304 lifts the async-expressions lane: async function expressions emit through the sync closure machinery with the async descriptor marker and blocking bodies, block-level async functions declare through the cell + anonymous-wrapper path, and an `await E;` statement evaluates exactly once with the await-site completion check and discards the value (the three jvm-async-fn-expr pins — typed local, callback, and returned first-class value — run with the completion check at every await).

tests.name: jvm-async-completion-int-boundary
tests.description: The await-site int completion check runs the emitted checkInt boundary: the maximal safe-range int (2^53-1) passes through the await and back out
tests.source:
async function big(): int { return 9007199254740991; }
export async function test(): int { return await big(); }

tests.name: jvm-async-error-propagation
tests.description: Completion failure: an awaited async function completing by raising E8005 propagates the error at the await site out of the caller (DEAL_ERROR_CODE, exit 1)
tests.source:
async function bomb(): int { return 1 / 0; }
export async function test(): int { return await bomb(); }

tests.name: jvm-async-nested-error-propagation
tests.description: An error raised by an awaited operation propagates through every enclosing await: innermost raises E8005, mid awaits innermost, test awaits mid — the error surfaces at the outermost await

tests.name: jvm-async-function-value
tests.description: An async function used as a value: a typed local holds the declared function's wrapper and an awaited indirect call through the variable returns 6

tests.name: jvm-async-function-value-callback
tests.description: A callback parameter of async function type: the declared function value passes into the parameter and the awaited indirect call dispatches through its wrapper (7)

tests.name: jvm-async-function-value-local-reassign
tests.description: A function-typed LOCAL of async function type: the binding holds wrapper references, reassignment swaps the wrapped function, and each awaited indirect call dispatches through the binding's current value (ab) — the v1.2 module shape (E1049) removed module-level fields, so the pre-rebase module-field version becomes a local reassignment

tests.name: jvm-async-multi-module
tests.description: Imported async direct calls through the real orchestrator pipeline: the entry module exports the v1.2 selected-entry non-async main(): null and awaits lib.tag (string completion) and lib.plus (int completion) across module boundaries in its auto-invoked async test export (5)

modules.lib.deal:
export async function plus(a: int, b: int): int { return a + b; }
export async function tag(s: string): string { return "[" + s + "]"; }

tests.name: jvm-async-lua-ref-reassigned-adapter
tests.description: LuaJIT reference semantics for the reassigned-local adapter shape hidden in an awaited call's argument list that the JVM slice conservatively rejects with E6000 (pinned in JvmBackendTest.testAsyncSlice): LuaJIT's adapter reads the binding live on every invoke, so g = two retargets the earlier async arity-extension adapter (await h(1, 2) = 11). The argument-hidden assignment form (apply(g = two, 1)) is not Lua-emittable — Lua has no assignment expressions in a call argument list — so the reference source uses the statement reassignment exactly like the sync sibling jvm-fv-lua-ref-reassigned-adapter, and the async adapter returns the inner operation handle with the completion check at the await site
